sources.title: Nightingale Dedicated Server documentation v0.8 (Inflexion Games)
How to Kick or Ban Players on a Nightingale Server - in-game Social Screen (O), Remove/Ban on the player card, unban by editing Bans= in ServerState.ini
Ekman/Nightingale-Docker - ServerSettings.ini keys (StartingDifficulty, Password, AdminPassword); AdminPassword 'grants access to the kick/ban commands'; no RCON
fireblade004/nightingale-server - Docker image configured by environment variables (MAXPLAYERS, CONNECTIONPASSWORD, SERVERGAMEPORT); no RCON or console
WindowsGSM.Nightingale plugin - 7777 UDP default / 27015 UDP query, no RCON (note: its README app-id field and -port=8211 line are copy-pasted from another plugin)
SteamDB - Nightingale Dedicated Server (app 3796810, type Tool)

notes: No command channel exists. Inflexion's official v0.8 guide documents the entire control surface as start-up command line / -ini arguments: -log, -noconsole, -port=<1024-65535>, -multihome=<ip>, -statusPort=<1024-65535>, -EnableCheats (cheat/debug menu), -ini:ServerSettings:[/Script/NWX.NWXServerSettings]:Password= / :AdminPassword=, -ini:Game:[/Script/Engine.GameSession]:MaxPlayers=, -ini:Engine:[JsonLogger]:bEnable=true / :bStdout=true, and -ini:Engine:[HTTPServer.Listeners]:+ListenerOverrides=(Port=<port>,BindAddress=<ip>) (a bind override for the status listener, NOT an admin API). The same keys can live in NWX/Config/ServerSettings.ini, copied from ExampleServerSettings.ini. There is no RCON, no stdin command console and no admin API. The guide states: 'If an admin password is set, players with the correct password can authenticate in-game in order to kick and ban other players' - moderation is a GUI action in the game client's social menu (join as admin, press O for the Social Screen, then Remove to kick or Ban on the player's card), and bans are recorded by player name on the Bans= line of NWX/Saved/Config/<Platform>Server/ServerState.ini, with no Steam ID or UID surfaced to target, which is why no playerId is recorded. The optional -statusPort flag adds a READ-ONLY HTTP endpoint, GET http://<host>:<port>/status, returning 503 {"status":"loading","player_count":0,"player_names":[]} while starting and 200 {"status":"ready","player_count":2,"player_names":["Alice","Bob"]} once up (names only, no identifiers, accepts no commands); it is recorded here in notes rather than as a rest transport because nothing can be sent to it. Linux entry point is NWXServer.sh; default game port UDP 7777, query port UDP 27015; server tool app id 3796810 (SteamDB, type Tool). Third-party hosting wikis (e.g. supercraft.host) publish a fabricated Nightingale command set (/kick, /ban, /unban, /tp, /shutdown, /save, /say, /players, /info, /help), as does a Steam forum reply suggesting the Minecraft command '/pardon-ip'; none of it exists and none must be ingested. Documentation fetched is version 0.8 - re-check if Inflexion publishes a newer PDF.
